deep.reconstruction:
The page is a coloured diagram drawn on the back of 1982 computer-listing paper, with a short caption. As elsewhere in cote 154, it concerns arrangements of pseudo-lines in the plane, or a disc / projective plane.

What the drawing shows:
(i) About ten yellow-green pseudo-lines. Their ends on the boundary ('bouts') are marked with short blue strokes.
(ii) Many crossings carry orange asterisk-like marks. These are probably the 'étoiles' (stars): vertices of the arrangement, possibly multiple points, drawn as several strands through a point.
(iii) Small blue shaded triangles at some crossings. These are probably triangular cells or marked vertices.
(iv) Short orange transversal ticks on some edges.
(v) A distinguished curve running diagonally through the arrangement, drawn in alternating dark green and brown segments.
(vi) Around this curve, an orange 'canal' (channel). It is a strip bounded by two orange curves and cross-hatched by rungs, like a ladder. The strip pinches to points at several vertices of the arrangement, and between pinches it swells into lens-shaped regions. One segment is drawn as a thick orange band.

The caption reads roughly: 'canaux ; : canaux [crossed-out word] — lieu des cours (courbes?) entre bouts (bleus) marqués, et étoiles exceptionnelles isolées (ou sous-étoiles).'

Modern reading: given an arrangement and two marked ends at infinity, Grothendieck considers the locus swept by all admissible 'courses' (pseudo-line-like curves) joining those ends. Admissible probably means they keep the pseudo-line axioms with respect to the existing lines: each old line is crossed exactly once.

This locus is the 'canal'. It is a chain of cells (the ladder rungs being the crossed edges). It is pinched at points where every such curve is forced through a vertex. These would be the 'étoiles exceptionnelles' (a forced passage through a star, or through a sub-star formed by a subset of the lines at a multiple point).

So the page explores the space of single-element extensions of a pseudo-line arrangement with prescribed ends. Equivalently, it explores the possible positions or isotopy of one line relative to the others. This is close to Levi's enlargement lemma, the zone of a line, and extension spaces of oriented matroids. The neighbouring pages (discs with D, D', marked ends x, y, x', y', hatched regions, local crossing pictures) are consistent with this: they study local moves and the passage of one line through regions of an arrangement.
errors: No mathematical claim is asserted beyond the caption, so there is nothing to check for correctness. The reading of the drawing (canal = locus of admissible curves between marked ends, pinches = forced vertices) is an interpretation.
One possible gap: whether such a locus is always a single chain of cells pinched only at vertices, rather than a more complicated region, is not argued on the page.

ideas.what: Arrangement of pseudo-lines with marked ends at infinity and marked (multiple) crossing points ('étoiles')
ideas.modern_name: pseudoline arrangement / wiring diagram; rank-3 oriented matroid

ideas.what: 'Canal': the locus of all admissible curves joining two prescribed ends through an arrangement. It is a strip of cells pinched at forced vertices.
ideas.modern_name: space of single-element extensions with prescribed ends; closely related to the zone of a line and to Levi's enlargement lemma
ideas.usually_credited_to: Levi (1926) for the existence of extensions; Las Vergnas, Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993) for extension spaces; Edelsbrunner et al. for the zone theorem

ideas.what: 'Étoiles exceptionnelles isolées (ou sous-étoiles)': vertices, or sub-bundles of lines through a multiple point, through which every admissible extending curve is forced to pass
ideas.modern_name: forced vertices / pinch points of the extension region; localizations or lifts through multiple points

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines a 'canal' as the region swept by all pseudo-line-type courses between two marked ends of an arrangement. He observes that it decomposes as a chain of lens-shaped regions pinched at exceptional stars or sub-stars. A precise statement is not written down: for example, a structure theorem for this region, or a criterion for when it is pinched.
missed.quote: canaux ; ... lieu des cours entre bouts (bleus) marqués, et étoiles exceptionnelles isolées (ou sous-étoiles)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A combinatorial description of the set of extensions with fixed points at infinity, including the forced vertices, connects to extension spaces of oriented matroids and to counting or enumerating arrangements. It is unclear that this exact 'channel with pinches' formulation is in the literature, but it is likely close to known material, so the novelty is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an illustrative diagram with a one-sentence definition of 'canaux' in the pseudo-line project. The notion is close to known ideas: extensions of arrangements, zones, Levi's lemma. It documents Grothendieck's private vocabulary rather than an evidently new result.
transcription_corrections: 'lieu des cours entre bouts' — the word read as 'cours' may be 'courbes' (curves). The meaning would be the locus of curves between marked ends.
The crossed-out word after 'canaux' is uncertain. 'huit' is doubtful; a superscript correction is written above it.
'isolées' is uncertain; the word may be 'installées' or similar. The reading '(ou sous-étoiles)' seems right.

The transcription omits the drawing: yellow-green pseudo-lines with blue-marked ends, orange star marks at crossings, blue shaded triangles, a dark green/brown distinguished curve, and an orange ladder-like channel around it with pinch points.
